searchText: <@!333694584607604738> I'm trying to run this faucet, but it requires a JSONRPC port. I started Besu with the information I found here: https://github.com/ethereum/eth1.0-specs/blob/master/network-upgrades/client-integration-testnets/aleut.md I get this right now: ``` ``` Do you have a node I can connect to on Aleut? Either JSONRPC port or enode. <@!500419996652929044> I currently connect via http://3.12.166.199:8545 thanks for looking into the faucet btw. - much appreciated! oh nice I'll try that hang on well I will get paid with your feedback on the faucet. Hope it's ok. sure thing - feedback is my favorite currency 😉 Feedback maximalist here <@333694584607604738> try here: http://aleut.tmio.io:8080/ 2 things. The faucet just requires you to sign in once to github and give your id, so we can avoid spamming and the faucet has its own wallet, its public key is 0xf4f90b306e9a1bff8097a8e37464a9d1a8d850da you can fund it the faucet behaves differently than most. It only tops off accounts if they are below a certain balance : 1 eth here. if it's less than 1 eth, it will top you up to 1 eth. I can change to a higher threshold. Faucet code is here: https://github.com/apache/incubator-tuweni/tree/main/eth-faucet Kotlin and Spring Boot. Enjoy! YAY Kotlin ❤️ but seeing this currently: I see this in the logs so first time, there was a problem, but since then, it went through? I do not see any funds arriving at the address: http://eip1559-testnet.ops.pegasys.tech:3000/account/0xdea872149f4d1f0041c4e87e82788fe6040d59fc that's because the faucet is empty: http://eip1559-testnet.ops.pegasys.tech:3000/account/0xf4f90b306e9a1bff8097a8e37464a9d1a8d850da (I don't have anything to do with Aleut, I have no eth on that network) ah ok - I can put some funds on the faucet later - don't have too much - but can fund a bit no problem. Hopefully that's clear - it's just a hot wallet sending transactions on demand github is the only auth though? I want to use it for a mobile wallet for end-users - not all will have github or want to enter their github credentials on mobile what would you want? something like this: https://goerli-faucet.slock.it/ ideally also with address passing via URL parameter I don't know how to make reCaptcha work 😦 I'm no good at frontend ah interesting <@!500419996652929044> thanks anyway! No problem. If you ever feel like it, you're welcome to file issues there: https://github.com/apache/incubator-tuweni/issues No pressure though. I am sending many eip1559 transactions on baikal. and one out of the three sealers makes empty blocks (I know it's not Besu) as just mentioned on the 1559-wallet-call (but it's a bit hard to visualize code just by speaking about it) - currently it is : 0x02 `||` rlp([chainId, nonce, maxPriorityFeePerGas, maxFeePerGas, gasLimit, to, value, data, access_list, signatureYParity, signatureR, signatureS]). if it would be 0x02 `||` rlp([chainId, nonce, maxPriorityFeePerGas, maxFeePerGas, access_list, gasLimit, to, value, data, signatureYParity, signatureR, signatureS]). a bigger section of the RLP list would be common between old and 1559 transactions which would make the code a bit nicer as the second ( gasLimit, to, value, data, signatureYParity, signatureR, signatureS) part could just be reused as it is the same as in the old transaction style. Or is there a reason access_list is on that position? cc <@!552133098075193354> This is the Geth node, if you check ethstats then you can also see that the txpool stays empty for that sealer I think it could be the Nethermind node. I'll check it tomorrow. <@!680337202521440470> is this possible to keep sending these transactions? It's definitely Geth Are you runnimg https://github.com/ethereum/go-ethereum/pull/22898 ? If not then please try this bramch.
